messages:
mel: Heads-up: I'm putting together a proposal to standardize OTEL bootstrap across py/go/rust inference services — single shape for resource attrs + per-tenant exporter routing. WDYT? :thinking:

ira: love it. main risk is lifecycle/shutdown differences across languages. py's global tracer problems are real.

sam: +1. also exporter retry/backpressure — we had OOMs last month when OTLP exporter blocked the event loop.

anya: we should avoid global init in library code. prefer explicit init in service main with a tiny shim helper (no heavy deps).

jordan: question: do we keep BatchSpanProcessor or implement an async/channel-based batcher for rust? rust + tokio semantics differ from go runtime.

mel: proposal sketch:
1) provide a small init lib per lang (redwood-otel-init) that sets resource attrs: service.name, env, model_id, deployment_id
2) accept env overrides for exporter endpoint, compression, and mode (noop/local_file/otlp)
3) default sampler: parentbased_probabilistic with low default (0.5%) but route-level overrides for high-signal routes

ira: nit: sampling should be workload-configurable via route metadata. high-qps model routes sample less; debugging routes can set 100%.

sam: practical constraints: in python we saw gevent + blocking exporter hangs. need non-blocking exporter with bounded queue + overflow policy (drop oldest) + telemetry metrics about drops.

anya: example env config snippet:
```yaml
REDWOOD_OTEL_ENDPOINT: otlp-intake.redwood.local:4317
REDWOOD_OTEL_SAMPLER_PCT: 0.5
REDWOOD_OTEL_BATCH_MAX_QUEUE: 10000
REDWOOD_OTEL_EXPORTER_BACKOFF_MS: 50-2000
REDWOOD_OTEL_MODE: otlp # noop | local_file | otlp
```

jordan: rust implementer here — async-batch with bounded mpsc channel + tokio spawn worker makes sense. also expose a sync flush on shutdown that waits up to Xs.

mel: also need to be careful with KV cache spans — don't log raw keys. add attributes: kv_cache.hit (bool) and kv_cache.prefix_len (int). redact key strings at init-time.

rusty: go implementer: go's otel sdk has resource detection at init, but it can be racey if accidentally initialized twice. we should export an InitOnce() helper and make it idempotent.

ira: retention and routing: tag spans with tenancy info (tenant_id, retention_tier) and let telemetry pipeline route to different retention buckets. for private deployments default to local_file or noop exporter.

mel: UX ask: console should surface dropped spans / exporter backpressure rates per service + per-route. add counters for dropped_spans, exporter_backpressure, exporter_5xx_rate.

devops-bot: alert: exporter endpoint otlp-prod in us-west had 5xx spike 2027-05-12T11:23Z (incid=RED-2027-238)

sam: +1 on console counters — and add 95th latency for exporter RPCs. also expose per-model sampled_ratio so infra can tune sample rates.

anya: small follow-up: avoid adding heavy deps in inference worker; init lib must be tiny, optional compile feature in rust.

mel: action items: @ira draft language-agnostic spec for attrs/sampling + examples; @jordan and @rusty produce minimal init shims for go/rust; @sam and @anya do python prototype. I'll open an RFC doc. timeline: prototype EOW.

ira: ack. I'll start with resource attr list and allowed env names.

jordan: FYI: I can push a PoC with go that wraps otel/sdk TraceProvider + Batcher in ~60 LOC.

sam: can we bake in a noop exporter for offline tests? saves a lot.

mel: yes. include `REDWOOD_OTEL_MODE: noop|local_file|otlp` default otlp in hosted.

jordan: re: attr keys, let's standardize on snake_case, not camel. e.g., model_id, route_id, sequence_len.

mel: thanks everyone. I'll post RFC link once created.
